note.question: How should managers and committees interpret overwhelming but potentially coordinated evidence, and can group deliberation or preference heterogeneity improve the truthful aggregation of private signals?
note.overview: The group treatments are communication-and-voting games in which publicly known preference heterogeneity creates strategic incentives to conceal private signals. The paper derives refined equilibrium communication and voting behavior with and without correlated signals, then tests the predictions experimentally. Correlation can restore a truth-telling equilibrium by creating an additional pivotal event shared by conflicting types.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Nature selects red state rho or blue state beta with equal prior probability and draws three imperfect signals. In individual treatments, one participant observes all three signals and chooses a state. In group treatments, each of three fixed group members privately observes one signal, simultaneously sends a red, blue, or nonrevealing white message in a modified straw poll, observes the other messages, and votes for rho or beta; simple majority determines the group decision. In the chat variation, members additionally send a recommendation and free-form rationale after the straw poll and before voting.

components.label: Equilibrium or solution concept
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Refined communication-and-majority-voting equilibria with aligned or heterogeneous preferences. Appendix B derives the equilibrium benchmark under rational selfish play and refinements that rule out payoff-irrelevant voting and excessive babbling. Homogeneous groups truthfully reveal signals and vote for the posterior-payoff-maximizing state. In heterogeneous groups without correlation, majority members reveal truthfully while the unbiased minority withholds information; with correlation, all members truthfully reveal and vote for the payoff-maximizing state because detecting the correlated all-blue event realigns incentives.
